ai.literal: Good natured you are, may you live, O Anicha flower! Than you, of softer nature is she whom I love.
ai.translation: May you live long, O Anicha flower, for you are indeed of a delicate nature! Yet, she whom I love is of an even softer nature than you.
ai.modern: அனிச்சப் பூவே! நீ நல்ல மென்மையான இயல்பைக் கொண்டிருக்கிறாய், நீ வாழ்க! ஆனால், நான் விரும்பும் என் காதலி உன்னை விடவும் மென்மையான இயல்புடையவள் ஆவாள்.
ai.explanation: The poet addresses the delicate Anicha flower, which is famous in classical Tamil literature for being so sensitive that it withers merely upon being smelled. He praises the flower's gentle nature and wishes it well. However, he immediately elevates his beloved above the flower, declaring that she whom he loves possesses a nature that is even softer and more delicate than the flower itself. This comparison beautifully highlights the supreme tenderness and grace of the beloved.

ai.literal: Flower if seen, you become bewildered, O heart, her eyes, many people see, flower resembles, thinking that.
ai.translation: O my heart! Whenever you see a flower, you become bewildered, thinking that her eyes resemble a common flower that is seen by everyone.
ai.modern: நெஞ்சமே! மலரைப் பார்க்கும்போதெல்லாம், 'இவளுடைய கண்கள் பலரும் பார்க்கின்ற இந்த மலரைப் போன்றதுதான்' என்று நினைத்து நீ மயங்குகிறாயே!
ai.explanation: In this couplet, the lover addresses his own heart, which gets excited and confused upon seeing a flower. The heart mistakenly compares the beloved's eyes to a common flower. The lover gently chides his heart, pointing out that the flower is something 'seen by many', whereas her eyes are unique and exclusive to him. By highlighting this contrast, the poet elevates the beauty and singularity of the beloved's eyes above ordinary nature.

ai.literal: Tender shoot complexion, pearl smile, fragrance scent, spear collyrium-painted eye, bamboo shoulder, to her.
ai.translation: For her of the bamboo-like shoulders, her complexion is a tender shoot, her smile is a pearl, her natural scent is fragrance itself, and her collyrium-painted eyes are spears.
ai.modern: மூங்கில் போன்ற தோள்களை உடைய அவளுக்கு, உடலின் நிறம் தளிர் போன்றது; புன்னகை முத்து போன்றது; இயற்கை மணம் நறுமணம் போன்றது; மை தீட்டிய கண்கள் வேல் போன்றன.
ai.explanation: In this verse, the lover praises the physical beauty of his beloved by comparing her features to exquisite natural elements. Her shoulders are smooth and shapely like bamboo, and her complexion has the soft, golden hue of a fresh tender shoot. Her bright smile is compared to lustrous pearls, and her natural body odor is described as pure fragrance. Finally, her sharp, collyrium-painted eyes are likened to deadly spears, capturing both their shape and their piercing impact on his heart.

ai.literal: If it sees, the blue water-lily, having drooped, the ground will look at, 'the eyes of her who wears excellent ornaments we do not equal' saying.
ai.translation: If the blue water-lily could see, it would droop its head and look down at the ground, saying, 'We can never equal the eyes of this beautifully adorned woman.'
ai.modern: நீலக் குவளை மலர் பார்க்கக் கூடுமானால், 'சிறந்த அணிகலன்களை அணிந்த இவளுடைய கண்களுக்கு நாம் இணையாக மாட்டோம்' என்று கூறி, தலைகவிழ்ந்து தரையைப் பார்க்கும்.
ai.explanation: In this verse, the lover praises the extraordinary beauty of his beloved's eyes. He personifies the blue water-lily, a flower traditionally compared to beautiful eyes in classical poetry. He suggests that if the flower possessed the power of sight, it would realize its own inferiority to her eyes. Overcome with shame, the lily would droop its head and stare at the ground in defeat.

ai.literal: Anicha flower, stalk without removing, she wore; for [her] waist, good will not sound drums.
ai.translation: She wore the delicate Anicha flower without removing its stem; now, only ominous drums, and not auspicious ones, will sound for her fragile waist.
ai.modern: அவள் அனிச்ச மலரின் காம்பைக் கிள்ளாமல் அப்படியே தலையில் சூடிக்கொண்டாள்; அதனால், அவளது மெல்லிய இடைக்கு நல்ல மங்கல ஒலிகள் ஒலிக்காது (இடை முறிந்துவிடும் என்பதால் சாவுப் பறையே ஒலிக்கும்).
ai.explanation: This couplet uses playful exaggeration to praise the extreme delicacy of the heroine's waist. The Anicha flower is famous in classical Tamil poetry for being so delicate that it wilts when merely smelled. The heroine has worn this flower in her hair, but she neglected to remove its tiny stem (kāl). The poet humorously suggests that even this microscopic extra weight is too heavy for her incredibly slender waist (nugappu, a variant of nusuppu), causing it to be on the verge of breaking. Consequently, instead of joyful, auspicious drums (nalla paṟai), only the solemn drums of ruin will sound for her waist.

ai.literal: The moon and the young woman's face not distinguishing, from their place, confused, the stars.
ai.translation: Unable to distinguish between the moon and this maiden's face, the stars are bewildered and wander from their stations.
ai.modern: நிலவையும் இந்த இளம்பெண்ணின் முகத்தையும் வேறுபடுத்தி அறிய முடியாமல், விண்மீன்கள் தங்கள் இடத்திலிருந்து நிலைதடுமாறி கலங்கி நிற்கின்றன.
ai.explanation: In this couplet, the lover praises the extraordinary beauty of his beloved's face by comparing it to the moon. He poetically suggests that her face is so bright and flawless that even the stars in the sky are thoroughly confused. Unable to tell which is the real moon and which is her face, the stars lose their bearings and wander from their designated places. The word 'அறியா' (not knowing) highlights this celestial confusion, elevating the heroine's beauty to a cosmic scale.

ai.literal: Like to the shining moon that has filled its diminished edge, is there a blemish on the face of the beloved woman?
ai.translation: Is there a blemish on the face of my beloved, like the dark spot found on the bright full moon that has filled out its crescent shape?
ai.modern: தேய்ந்த பகுதி நிறைந்து விளங்கும் முழு நிலவுக்கு இருப்பது போல, என் காதலியின் முகத்தில் ஏதேனும் களங்கம் இருக்கிறதா?
ai.explanation: In this verse, the lover praises the flawless beauty of his beloved's face by comparing it to the moon. He notes that even the bright, fully formed moon has a visible dark spot or blemish on its surface. However, when he looks at his beloved's face, he asks rhetorically if there is any such blemish to be found. By highlighting this contrast, he exalts her beauty as something even more perfect and spotless than the full moon itself.

ai.literal: If you are capable of emitting light like the face of my beloved, you would be loved; may you live, O Moon!
ai.translation: O Moon, may you live long! If you can shine with the same radiant beauty as my beloved's face, then you too will be dear to me.
ai.modern: நிலவே, நீ வாழ்க! என் காதலியின் முகத்தைப் போல உன்னால் ஒளி வீச முடியுமானால், நீயும் எனக்கு அன்பிற்குரியவள் ஆவாய்.
ai.explanation: In this couplet, the lover addresses the moon with a playful challenge. He begins with a polite blessing, 'வாழி மத஧' (may you live long, O Moon), but immediately sets a condition for his affection. He says that the moon will only be dear to him ('காதலை') if it is capable ('வல்லையேல்') of shining with the same exquisite splendor as his beloved's face ('மாதர் முகம்போல் ஒளிவிட'). By placing the beauty of his beloved's face above the natural brilliance of the moon, the poet beautifully illustrates the lover's intense adoration.

ai.literal: If you resemble the face of her who has flower-like eyes, do not appear for many to see, O Moon!
ai.translation: O Moon! If you wish to resemble the face of my beloved who has flower-like eyes, do not rise in the sky for everyone to see.
ai.modern: மலரைப் போன்ற கண்களை உடையவளின் முகத்திற்கு நீ ஒப்பாக விரும்பினால், நிலவே! பலர் பார்க்கும்படி வானில் தோன்றாதே.
ai.explanation: In this couplet, the hero playfully addresses the moon, comparing its beauty to his beloved's face. He tells the moon that if it truly wishes to equal the beauty of her face, which is graced with flower-like eyes, it must not show itself in public. By rising in the open sky where everyone can gaze at it, the moon's spots and imperfections are easily noticed, making the comparison fail. Therefore, the hero advises the moon to remain hidden to preserve any claim of resembling her flawless beauty.

ai.literal: The anicham flower and the swan's feathers, to the beloved woman's feet, are nerunji thorns.
ai.translation: Both the delicate anicham flower and the soft down of a swan are as harsh as the thorny nerunji fruit to the tender feet of my beloved.
ai.modern: அனிச்ச மலரும் அன்னப் பறவையின் மென்மையான இறகுகளும் என் காதலியின் மெல்லிய பாதங்களுக்கு நெருஞ்சி முள் போன்றவையாகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet uses poetic exaggeration to praise the extreme tenderness of the beloved's feet. The speaker claims that even the softest elements of nature, such as the delicate anicham flower and the downy feathers of a swan, would feel like the sharp, painful thorns of the nerunji fruit if they touched her feet. By contrasting these famously soft objects with a prickly thorn, the verse highlights the incomparable delicacy of her form. This comparison serves to express the lover's deep adoration and protective concern.
